title: Terahertz generation through photon deceleration of long-wavelength infrared laser pulses in plasma

crossref.abstract: <jats:p>We study the convective parametric amplification of the scattered wave driven by a spatially localized broadband pump in an inhomogeneous plasma in one-dimensional geometry. Two particular cases are considered: a strongly inhomogeneous plasma, in which the three-wave interaction length is shorter than the pump localization length; and a tightly focused laser beam, in which the localization length is shorter than the detuning length due to plasma inhomogeneity. A numerical solution of a pair of coupled-wave equations shows that, in both cases, the broadband pump produces a strongly nonstationary response, with large-amplitude spikes in the scattered-wave intensity. However, the time-averaged level of scattered intensity is reproducible across simulations with different pump field realizations. It shows relatively small statistical variation when the pump bandwidth exceeds the characteristic growth rate of the instability. The pump bandwidth leads to a notable difference between the forward and backward scattering (for the same characteristic growth rate). Backward-scattering amplification is smaller, and it exhibits a stronger dependence on the pump bandwidth. Conditions for mitigating spatial amplification are discussed for stimulated Raman and Brillouin scattering.</jats:p>
title: Excitation of parametric instabilities with a broadband laser pulse in an inhomogeneous plasma

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Laser plasma accelerators (LPAs), capable of producing ultra-short, high peak current electron beams with low emittance, offer a promising path toward next-generation compact free-electron lasers (FELs). However, their large energy spread, high divergence, and shot-to-shot fluctuations present major challenges for stable FEL operation. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of the
                    <jats:sc>Coxinel</jats:sc>
                    phase-space manipulation beamline in mitigating these limitations for 196 MeV LPA-generated electron beams, with beam transport validated through experiments and
                    <jats:sc>Elegant</jats:sc>
                    simulations. FEL performance at 270 nm is analyzed using
                    <jats:sc>Genesis</jats:sc>
                    code, with additional studies extending to shorter wavelength (64 nm, 41 nm, 28 nm), revealing strong sensitivity to beam parameters at the LPA source. The results establish a structured approach for optimizing LPA-driven FELs, highlighting key advances in beam transport, stability, and phase-space control for compact light sources.
                  </jats:p>
title: Qualifying LPA generated electron beams to free electron laser applications

citation_title: Radiation in relativistic plasmas via particle simulations
citation_abstract: We investigate radiation in relativistic electron-proton isotropic plasmas using molecular dynamics, with velocity-dependent inertia, retarded interactions, and quantum-corrected pair potentials. Radiation spectra from the Li\'enard-Wiechert fields agree with analytical models. Successive scattering events suppress bremsstrahlung even at weak coupling, while jitter radiation becomes comparable at higher coupling for all resolved frequencies. This first-principles framework will help develop radiation models for suppression and field effects that are inaccessible in typical particle-in-cell methods.

citation_title: Fuse-PINN: Combining Finite Element Methods and Physics-Informed Neural Networks to enable massively parallel simulations of non-linear PDEs
citation_abstract: Research in the domain of Physics-Informed Neural Networks applied to PDE modelling has advanced significantly in recent years, providing a wide ecosystem of novel methods. However, one frequent limitation is the inability of PINNs to scale out on High-Performance Computing architectures to address more ambitious challenges, particularly non-linear physics models with turbulent dynamics in large spatial domains. Typical studies restrain demonstrations to toy models with simple physics equations, few variables, and rarely any complex non-linear dynamics evolved over long timescales. Part of the AI community has even adopted the idea that "PINNs don't scale". This work proves otherwise. We present a mathematically robust formulation of Finite-Element-Method for Neural Networks (FEM-NN) implemented into a comprehensive, modular framework: Fuse-PINN. This formulation provides the basis for a sclable parallelisation of Physics-Informed Neural Networks on GPU-based HPC systems. Furthermore, an Energy Natural Gradient Descent optimiser is implemented to allow high-precision convergence. Fuse-PINN is demonstrated on physics models relevant to Magnetic Confinement Fusion, including non-linear convective models with fine-scale dynamics. Near-perfect scaling is achieved on multi-GPU runs with increasing problem size.
